title: Linda’s Tuna Tartare with Wasabi and Lime
source: From Linda  ·  Every family holiday gathering
headnote: Linda’s tuna tartare has become a beloved appetizer at every family holiday gathering. She buys her tuna at Stiles Market in Westport.

items.raw: 1 teaspoon wasabi paste, or more to taste
Flaky salt and freshly ground black pepper
1 avocado or ½ English cucumber, thinly sliced (optional)

steps.text: Work with a very sharp knife and cold fish. Cut the tuna into ¼-inch dice — chopped, not minced. You want to feel the pieces. Keep it in a bowl set over ice while you make the dressing.

Whisk the soy sauce, sesame oil, lime juice, wasabi, and ginger together in a small bowl until the wasabi dissolves completely. Taste it now, before it hits the fish, and adjust the wasabi — it should be sharp enough to make you blink.
Pour the dressing over the tuna and add the scallions and cilantro. Fold gently with a rubber spatula, just enough to coat. Season with a little salt and pepper.
Cover and refrigerate 15 to 20 minutes. Any longer and the lime and soy begin to cure the fish, turning it opaque and firm.
Lay the crackers out on a platter. Top each with a slice of avocado or cucumber if using, then a small spoonful of tartare. Scatter the sesame seeds over everything.
Crackers go soft within about fifteen minutes, so bring the platter out the moment it is built. Any leftover tartare can be served in a small bowl with crackers alongside.

notes.label: Where to buy
notes.text: Linda gets hers at Stiles Market in Westport. Ask for a center-cut piece of yellowfin or bigeye and tell them it is for tartare. If it smells like anything but clean ocean, do not buy it.

notes.label: Ahead of time
notes.text: the dressing can be made a day ahead. Chop and dress the tuna no more than 30 minutes before serving.

notes.label: Variations
notes.text: a small dice of ripe mango adds sweetness against the wasabi. A few drops of chili oil over the finished platter is also very good.

notes.label: Raw fish
notes.text: skip it for anyone pregnant, elderly, or immune-compromised.

notes.label: Serving in a bowl
notes.text: for a less fussy version, mound the tartare in a chilled bowl, ring it with crackers, and let people build their own.
